sources.title: Foundation of Lahore Darbar or Sikh Empire and British Approaches
sources.note: Scholarly study distinguishing the 1799 foundation at Lahore, later diplomacy, and the longer 1799 to 1849 state history.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Lahina Singh
sources.note: Punjabi University reference on the Lahore triumvirate, 1765 occupation, administration, forces, revenue, and Lahina Singh death.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Gujjar Singh Bhangi
sources.note: Punjabi University reference on divided Lahore, the eastern settlement, mud fort, wells, mosque, family alliance, and 1788 death.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Qila Gujjar Singh
sources.note: Punjabi University place reference on the Bhangi partition, eastern enclave, gateway, size, and continuing relationship to Lahore.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Shah Zaman
sources.note: Punjabi University reference on the 1797 and 1798 Durrani occupations, retreats, fighting, and wider succession crisis.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Sada Kaur Sardarni
sources.note: Punjabi University biography establishing Sada Kaur leadership, resources, joint command, and the 7 July 1799 Lahore capture.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Bagh Singh Virk
sources.note: Punjabi University biography of a nearby chief whose later accommodation shows layered authority around Lahore.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Anarkali
sources.note: Punjabi University reference locating Ranjit Singh headquarters in the Anarkali garden during the 1799 operation.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Saundha Singh
sources.note: Punjabi University biography documenting study of Hindi, Rekhta, Persian, and music near Chunian in Lahore district.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Historiography of Afghanistan
sources.note: Scholarly account of the 1798 Tarikh-e Hosaynshahi, whose author joined Shah Zaman at Lahore and described Durrani administration and army.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Sir John Malcolm
sources.note: Scholarly account of British fears about Zaman Shah and the 1799 to 1801 diplomatic mission to Qajar Iran.

sources.title: State Bank of Pakistan Museum: Sikh Rulers and Coinage
sources.note: Official museum account of misl coinage, Lahore mint, Persian legends, standards, and the 1799 political transition.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Nur ud-Din Faqir
sources.note: Punjabi University biography securely dating Ranjit Singh assumption of the Maharaja title and Lahore dispensary appointments to 1801.

sources.title: British Museum: Lahore-minted Sikh Misal rupee, 1792
sources.note: Museum object record for a silver Sikh Misal rupee dated 1792 and minted at Lahore.

sources.title: Paramdip Kaur Khera, Catalogue of Sikh Coins in the British Museum
sources.note: British Museum Research Publication 190 with catalogued Lahore coin dates, Persian legends, transliteration, translation, weights, and mints.

sources.title: History of the Origin and Progress of the Sicks, 1787
sources.note: Contemporary English-language account with cautious evidence on Sikh coin language, assemblies, mobility, food, and political organization.

sources.title: Pakistan Archaeology, number 1: Lahore excavations
sources.note: Federal archaeology report on stratified Lahore deposits and Islamic-period pottery, oil lamps, basins, pitchers, jar covers, and porcelain.

sources.title: Department of Archaeology and Museums: Lahore Fort
sources.note: Official federal monument record for the fort, inherited Mughal spaces, later Sikh use, additions, materials, and functions.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Fort and Shalamar Gardens in Lahore
sources.note: Authoritative description of Lahore Fort and Shalamar Gardens, their water design, surviving monuments, chronology, and cultural synthesis.

sources.title: MIT Aga Khan Program: Conservation of the Walled City of Lahore
sources.note: Academic conservation case study on walls, gates, trade-route location, urban decline, climate, and later infrastructure.

sources.title: Traditional Urban Houses of Lahore
sources.note: Peer-reviewed architectural study of courtyard houses, cul-de-sacs, privacy, tarra platforms, and later surviving urban morphology.

sources.title: Walled City of Lahore Authority: Monuments
sources.note: Official provincial heritage account of the Shahi Hammam, Lahore collections, and the Bhangi triumvirate before 1799.

sources.title: Walled City of Lahore Authority: Lahore Fort
sources.note: Official site history distinguishing inherited Mughal buildings from additions during Ranjit Singh rule beginning in 1799.

sources.title: Walled City of Lahore Authority: Akbari Hamam
sources.note: Official description of a royal bath with water and steam channels, used to distinguish bathing technology from citywide sanitation.

sources.title: British Library Mss Eur F22: Mughal Beg journey reports
sources.note: Archive catalog for Persian reports made in 1790 about journeys through Punjab, northwestern India, Afghanistan, and Central Asia.

sources.title: British Library Add MS 17952: Karabadin-e Qadiri
sources.note: Archive record for a Persian materia medica according to Indian practice, copied in 1790.

sources.title: Library of Congress: Mizan al-tibb
sources.note: Digitized Persian medical teaching text widely used by students from the eighteenth century, with explicit purpose and limits.

sources.title: Wellcome Collection: Persian medical dictionary, MS Persian 77
sources.note: Public-domain eighteenth-century Persian manuscript describing simple and compound medicines in professional Shikastah script.

sources.title: Journal of Punjab Studies: Issues of Gender and Sikhs
sources.note: Scholarly discussion of late eighteenth-century Sikh women holding estates, making grants, and acting in administration and politics.

sources.title: Sikhs in the Eighteenth Century
sources.note: Scholarly collection on misl organization, village specialization, exchange, marriage links, leadership, and the limits of centralized rule.

sources.title: The Indian Merchant Diaspora in Early Modern Central Asia and Iran
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study placing Punjabi and Khatri merchants within wider commercial networks without reducing Lahore to one community.

sources.title: Public Health in Colonial Lahore, 1849 to 1910
sources.note: University thesis documenting later roof latrines, drains, water problems, and nineteenth-century reforms, used only as a non-back-projection control.

sources.title: Harvard GSD regional report on preserving historic Lahore
sources.note: Academic urban conservation report describing the historic city as a dense repository of shrines, houses, monuments, and working fabric.
